summary.title: Command Line Applications in Rust
summary.one_liner: An introductory book on building command line applications in Rust, starting with a quick tutorial that produces a working CLI tool and then covering CLI aspects in more depth.
takeaways: Rust suits command line apps because they should be small, portable, and quick to run.
Building a simple CLI is a good beginner exercise for learning Rust.
The book starts with a quick tutorial that yields a working CLI tool.
Later chapters explore CLI aspects in more detail after the tutorial introduces core Rust concepts.
summary.summary: This online book introduces building command line applications in Rust. It argues that Rust's static compilation, speed, and tooling make it a good fit for small, portable, fast CLI programs, and that CLI projects are a good way to learn the language. The book opens with a quick tutorial that produces a working CLI tool, introducing core Rust concepts, and then follows with chapters that go deeper into CLI topics. The page text provided is only the introduction, so the specific tools and libraries covered are not shown here.
